conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I’m Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you tonight. I understand you had a fall earlier?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I just got home from physical therapy and tripped over my pants in the bathroom. I hit my head on the wall.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. Did you lose consciousness or feel dizzy before the fall?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, I didn’t black out. I was just tired and hadn’t eaten. But I’m okay now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve checked a CT scan of your head and neck. Good news — there’s no fracture or bleeding in the brain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, that’s a relief. But why do I need to stay overnight?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We want to monitor you because of your history of falls and heart condition. Also, your kidney function was a bit off, and potassium was low.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: My kidneys? I thought that was from the diuretics I take.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Your creatinine is up a little — from your usual 1.6 to 2.0. That suggests mild dehydration. We’re holding your metolazone for now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So I won’t take it while I’m here?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Correct. And we’re adjusting your dose going forward — from three times a week to twice — to protect your kidneys.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs this morning look stable. Your potassium improved to 3.5, and white count is high but normal for you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve always had high white blood cells — my hematologist says it’s chronic.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that’s noted. Also, your urine showed some white cells, but you have no symptoms, so we won’t treat it as infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the spot on my chest X-ray? Is that pneumonia?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s likely atelectasis — a small area of collapsed lung — common after reduced activity. No fever or breathing issues, so no antibiotics needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re clearing you to go home today. Staples in your scalp should be checked in about 10 days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. I miss my dog. Will I need to change anything else at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Keep taking your usual heart and blood pressure meds. We increased your prednisone slightly — from 5mg to 10mg — for your platelet condition.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And the potassium pill?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, continue that daily, but stop it if your potassium goes above 4.0 — we’ll check that soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my heart failure clinic?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, follow up there. They’ll monitor your weight and kidney function. Call if you gain more than 3 pounds in a day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for explaining everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Stay safe, and take your time getting dressed — maybe sit down next time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll do that. And I’ll ask my son to help me rearrange the bathroom.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Excellent idea. We’ll have your son called to take you home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m ready. Thanks again.
